initial_scene: Robot-centered downward-facing view with both forearms emerging from below the camera. A red pepper and a green apple sit on the black upper shelf; the white bottom shelf is empty. Both hands are initially open beside the rack.

observed_sequence.action: Right arm rises from beside the rack and reaches toward the red pepper; left arm remains at the lower left without contacting the rack or objects.
Right hand surrounds and closes around the red pepper on the black upper shelf.
Right hand lifts the pepper from the upper shelf and carries it toward and beyond the right edge; the green apple remains on the shelf.
Right arm moves the held pepper downward outside the right side of the rack, then inward over the white bottom shelf.
Right hand lowers the pepper onto the bottom shelf while remaining wrapped around it; exact first shelf-contact frame is partly occluded.
Right fingers open; pepper is released and lies on the white bottom shelf while the hand remains immediately above it.

arm_hand_roles.right: Sole manipulating hand: reaches, grasps, lifts, transports, lowers and releases the red pepper.
arm_hand_roles.left: Remains open beside the rack and performs no object or rack support.

anatomical_side_evidence.evidence: The initial robot-centered view looks forward and downward between paired forearms extending from the robot beneath the camera. The active forearm can be followed continuously from the lower-right robot-side attachment toward the upper shelf; the opposite forearm remains at lower left. This egocentric orientation establishes active anatomical right rather than applying a front-facing image-side reversal.
anatomical_side_evidence.limitations: Shoulders and torso are largely outside the image; side is established from the paired near-body arm origins and robot-centered viewing direction.

coordination: No bimanual manipulation or person interaction; right hand completes the transfer alone.
terminal_state: Red pepper lies on the white bottom shelf following visible finger opening; right hand remains just above it. Green apple remains on the black upper shelf. Left hand stays open beside the rack.
uncertainties: Exact first contact between the pepper and bottom shelf is partly hidden by the right hand; release and pepper resting on the shelf are visible at the end.
